narrative_purpose: The cutaway shows why cetacean culture is an inference assembled from partial methods: each instrument samples one narrow window while the social life continues below.
subject: A clean ocean cutaway showing non-invasive field research methods. At the surface floats a small unbranded sailboat, with one slender hydrophone cable descending into the midwater, a compact observation drone hovering in the air above, and a small suction-cup tracking tag attached safely to a whale swimming below. A pod of five anatomically correct Earth whales glides through deep water in social formation. A small glass biopsy vial rests near a clean water sample; the scene is pure naturalist observation.
scene: Open ocean from air through surface to deep water, with the research layer occupying the top quarter and the largely hidden pod filling the lower half.
camera: Straight-on educational cutaway, wide aspect, surface line horizontal and each instrument physically connected to the part of the scene it samples.
light: Cyan daylight filtered through water, teal instrument glints, deep indigo lower ocean and sparse amber highlights on sampling points.
palette: Cool indigo-teal ocean, cyan sampling details, muted stone-grey boat and animals, sparse amber markers.
style: Painterly field-method naturalist plate with clear spatial organization, not a vector diagram.
detail_level: Crisp boat, drone, hydrophone, tag and nearest whales; deep social group softens into haze while remaining legible.
composition: Horizontal surface divides the frame; four sampling windows are distributed without overlap and large dark margins remain framed by deep negative space.
consistency_notes: Every method must be visually distinct and non-invasive. The image teaches partial access, so no single instrument should appear to reveal the entire pod or mind.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no infographic chrome, no military equipment, no injury, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon style
